note: What an endpoint-keyed mark may claim, and what has to be true of what it captured. A mark is `rb:<kind> <selector>[,<selector>...] [<key>=<value>...]`, closed by `rb:end` where the block rule would stop short of what the author meant. A selector is family.endpoint for one, family.* for all of a family, or * for the target. harness/snippets.py reads this file and never learns a kind's name, so adding one is an object under `kinds` and a display section. A kind is required "every" (a conformance target has to locate one for each endpoint), "declared" (spec/matrix.json says per family whether there is anything to show), "ratchet" (absence is counted against the allowance, never gated) or "never". The assertions are counted against the allowance rather than gated red: they fail on most of the corpus today and a red gate would block every branch that is fixing them. An allowance only ever goes down. --ratchet rewrites it from what the tree does, --check fails on anything above it.

handler.what: the lines that answer the request

wiring.what: the code that makes a feature family work, which the route does not name

test.what: the assertion that holds this target to the contract it declares

not_only_annotations.label: annotation-only
not_only_annotations.what: a snippet may not be nothing but annotations, attributes and comments
not_only_annotations.why: @Get("/json/small") names the route, passes both coverage checks, and says nothing about what answers the request

reaches_domain.label: not reaching the domain
reaches_domain.what: a handler and its support together must name something the shared domain gave the file
reaches_domain.why: a registration that names a handler defined elsewhere is complete, correct, and shows a reader nothing. The shared domain is where the behaviour is, so a snippet that never gets there has not captured the endpoint. The exception is baseline.plaintext, which has no domain to reach: it returns a literal

mentions_dep.label: wiring that does not name its dependency
mentions_dep.what: the support parts for a family must mention the dependency spec/matrix.json declares for it
mentions_dep.why: a mark that drifted onto neighbouring lines stops mentioning it, and a present mark is otherwise indistinguishable from a correct one

no_test.label: endpoint with no test
no_test.what: every endpoint has to be held by at least one test in its target's own suite, marked for it by name. A helper marked for its family or for the whole target is not a test of it
no_test.why: required: "every" is the right shape and cannot be used. harness/snippets.py drops a record that lacks a kind marked every, so setting it empties the snippet map for all fifty endpoints on all thirty-three targets and the site renders nothing at all. required: "ratchet" counts the endpoints with no test instead and holds the count against the allowance, which only ever goes down. The filter stays keyed to handler alone

reads_expectation.label: test that does not read the expectation
reads_expectation.what: a test marked for an endpoint by name has to name it, which is the key spec/expected.json is read by. A helper marked for a family or the target cannot name every endpoint it serves and is not asked to
reads_expectation.why: spec/expected.json is the only authority on what a correct answer is, and a status or a body written into a test as a literal is how 1,650 assertions drift away from it. Naming the endpoint is what a lookup looks like in every language, and it catches the second thing mentions_dep catches: a mark that drifted onto neighbouring lines stops naming its endpoint, and a drifted mark is otherwise indistinguishable from a correct one
